name: Plumber, Pipefitter and Sprinkler Fitter
description: ⚠⚠ A paid-apprenticeship trade: BLS describes 4 to 5 years of apprenticeship with about 2,000 paid hours a year, on a high school diploma. ⚠⚠⚠ Florida pays well below the national figure ($52,910 median against $63,800), and the gap widens to $34,810 at the 90th percentile. Florida's journeyman licence is issued locally but recognised in every county and city, and the contractor licence is the step that changes income.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ TWO LEVELS OF LICENCE. The JOURNEYMAN licence is issued by counties and municipalities, and under s. 489.1455, F.S. every other Florida county and municipality must recognise it. The conditions include a proctored journeyman examination, a registered and state-approved apprenticeship or at least 12,000 hours of on-the-job training, and Florida Building Commission coursework. ⚠ The CONTRACTOR licence is state-issued under chapter 489: certified (any Florida jurisdiction) or registered (only where registered). To sit the certification exam, one route is 4 years of experience through an apprenticeship with at least 1 year as a foreman (s. 489.111). ⚠ A school certificate does not replace the hours. Choose a registered apprenticeship if you can, because it counts directly toward the journeyman licence.

⚠ HVAC/R Engineering Technology — where Florida files HVAC; shares piping skills and the same journeyman reciprocity provision as plumbing (s. 489.1455).

courses.reason: Helper, Plumber, Pipefitter — occupational completion point A, 360 hours, at ten public institutions. ⚠⚠ A hireable exit named after the job: a plumber's helper can start work here and continue into an apprenticeship.

courses.reason: Residential Plumber — completion point B, 240 hours, at eleven institutions. Houses: water supply, drain-waste-vent systems, fixtures and water heaters.
Commercial Plumber — completion point C, 240 hours, at eleven institutions. Larger systems, commercial fixtures and code requirements for public buildings.

Plumber — completion point D, 120 hours, at eight institutions, and the end of the 960-hour ladder. ⚠ Ask whether the college awards a certificate at each point, since not every school issues the intermediate ones.
Plumbing Applications — 240 hours at Miami Dade, Palm Beach State and Pinellas Technical. ⚠ Applied practice beyond the four completion points; check where it sits in your college's sequence.

Plumbing Apprenticeship I — the first of the classroom courses that run alongside a paid registered apprenticeship, at the College of the Florida Keys, Indian River, Miami Dade, Santa Fe and South Florida State. ⚠⚠ This is the route most plumbers take: BLS describes a 4- or 5-year apprenticeship with about 2,000 paid hours of work a year.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Hours per course differ widely between colleges (about 33 to 99 for the same number). Daytona State pairs each level with a separate on-the-job lab (BCA0450L onward).

courses.reason: Plumbing Apprenticeship II — six carriers, including Daytona State.

Plumbing Apprenticeship IV — five carriers. ⚠ Around the middle of the sequence. The journeyman provision in s. 489.1455 counts a completed registered apprenticeship, or at least 12,000 hours of on-the-job training.

Plumbing Apprenticeship VIII — five carriers, the last level in the common sequence. ⚠ Completing a registered and state-approved apprenticeship is one of the routes to a journeyman licence that other Florida counties and municipalities must recognise (s. 489.1455).

Industrial Pipefitter Helper — completion point A of the industrial pipefitter programme, 300 hours, at Hillsborough and Manatee Technical. ⚠ Process piping in plants and industrial sites, a branch of the same SOC occupation.
Industrial Pipefitter — completion point B, 300 hours, at the same two institutions.

Fire Sprinkler Apprenticeship I — Hillsborough, Miami Dade and Seminole State, the first of a sequence that continues through BCA0477 and advanced levels. ⚠⚠ Sprinklerfitters are part of this occupation, and BLS expects their employment to grow because of building codes in all states that require fire suppression systems.

bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ An apprenticeship trade: you are paid while you learn

Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (47-2152)
Entry-level education (BLS)high school diploma
Training (BLS)⚠⚠ apprenticeship — “a 4- or 5-year apprenticeship” with “2,000 hours of paid on-the-job training, as well as some technical instruction, each year”
Median, 2025$63,800
Jobs510,600
Outlook 2025–35+7% (+34,500)
Openings a yearabout 42,000
Self-employed8%

⚠⚠ The normal route into plumbing is a job, not a classroom. An apprentice is hired, paid, and learns on site under a licensed plumber, with evening or block classes alongside. A school certificate can come first and shorten the start, but the licences that matter are earned with hours in the trade.

⚠ BLS gives two sources of demand: “new construction and … the need to maintain and repair plumbing systems in existing residences and other buildings,” and for sprinklerfitters, “building codes in all states that require the use of fire suppression systems.” BLS does not mention automation or AI for this occupation. The hazards it names are cuts, burns from hot pipes and soldering, and falls from ladders.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida pays plumbers well below the national figure, and the gap widens at the top

PercentileFloridaUnited StatesDifference
10th$38,940$44,150−$5,210
25th$47,220$50,190−$2,970
Median$52,910$63,800−$10,890
⚠ 75th$62,820$85,110⚠ −$22,290
⚠⚠ 90th$73,610$108,420⚠⚠ −$34,810

⚠⚠ The national figures describe a trade where experienced plumbers reach six figures. In Florida’s wage data the 90th percentile is $73,610. These figures cover employees only, so a Florida plumber who becomes a licensed contractor and runs a business is not measured here. That is the step that changes income, and it is licensed by the state (below). ⚠ When comparing job offers, ask about the pay scale for journeymen, not just for apprentices.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida licenses at two levels, and the journeyman licence travels

LevelWho issues itWhat it takes
Journeyman plumber⚠ counties and municipalities (s. 489.1455, F.S.)a proctored journeyman examination, a registered and state-approved apprenticeship or at least 12,000 hours of on-the-job training, and coursework approved by the Florida Building Commission
Certified plumbing contractorthe state (DBPR, Construction Industry Licensing Board) — valid in any Florida jurisdictionan examination; to sit it, for example four years of experience learned through an apprenticeship, “at least 1 year of active experience shall be as a foreman” (s. 489.111)
Registered plumbing contractorthe state, on the strength of a local competency licence“may contract only in such jurisdictions” (s. 489.105)

⚠⚠⚠ The journeyman licence is local, but Florida makes it portable. Under s. 489.1455, “counties and municipalities must recognize a person as a journeyman in the plumbing, pipe fitting, mechanical, or HVAC trades if the person was issued a journeyman license in such trade by a county or municipality in the state.” ⚠ That section names plumbing, pipe fitting, mechanical and HVAC. It does not name electrical, so check whether a journeyman licence moves with you if you work in more than one trade.

⚠ 12,000 hours is six years at the 2,000 hours a year BLS describes for an apprentice. The registered-apprenticeship route counts instead, which is one practical reason to choose a registered programme over an informal helper job.

⚠⚠ A plumbing contractor’s licence is broad. Florida’s definition covers water supply, sanitary drainage, septic tanks, swimming-pool piping, irrigation, solar water heating, medical gas, fire sprinklers and fuel-oil piping (s. 489.105).

⚠⚠ Two ways in, and Florida teaches both

1. The school certificate first. Florida’s clock-hour plumbing programme is built from four occupational completion points named after jobs — each a place to stop, be hired and come back:

CourseCompletion pointHoursPublic carriers
BCV0508 Helper, Plumber, PipefitterA36010
BCV0540 Residential PlumberB24011
BCV0562 Commercial PlumberC24011
BCV0592 PlumberD1208

That is 960 hours through completion point D. ⚠ The plumbing programme is at about ten public institutions; the equivalent electrician helper course (BCV0603) is at 26. A student outside the larger metro areas may find the plumbing certificate is not offered nearby, and should look at the apprenticeship route instead.

2. The registered apprenticeship. Several state colleges run the classroom half of plumbing apprenticeships as a numbered sequence, BCA0450–BCA0457 Plumbing Apprenticeship I–VIII, at Daytona State, the College of the Florida Keys, Indian River, Miami Dade, Santa Fe and South Florida State, while the apprentice works for a sponsoring employer. Fire sprinkler fitters have their own sequence (BCA0470 onward) at Hillsborough, Miami Dade and Seminole State. ⚠ The hours per course vary a great deal between colleges (from about 33 to 99 hours for the same number), so ask how many classroom hours your programme actually includes.

⚠ Ask any apprenticeship programme whether it is registered with the state. The journeyman provision above counts a “registered and state-approved apprenticeship program”; an informal helper job counts only through the 12,000 hours.

Where Florida trains plumbers

Programme (CIP)Credentials a yearWhere
Plumbing Technology (46.0503)144 at 21 institutionsOrange Technical West 25, Fort Myers Technical 19, Sheridan Technical 13, Hillsborough 12, Daytona State 12, Pinellas Technical 12, Miami Lakes 11, Suncoast Technical 11, Erwin Technical 11 …
Pipefitting and Sprinkler Fitting (46.0502)45 at 5Lively Technical 17, Seminole State 17, Hillsborough 7, Miami Dade 2, Orange Technical South 2

⚠⚠ About 189 credentials a year at 22 institutions, against roughly 42,000 openings a year nationally. School certificates are a small part of how Florida produces plumbers. Most learn through apprenticeships and on-the-job training, which IPEDS does not count.
